pr.title: Introduce a native management API and modern panel foundation
pr.body:
Phase 1b needs a modern panel and REST API without routing web administration through COM. Add an ASP.NET Core/.NET 10 host that reaches the C++ business layer through an opt-in, restricted local named pipe. Keep COM as an independent compatibility adapter sharing credential validation; existing tools and scripts retain their interface.

The foundation includes protected server-side sessions, CSRF/origin checks, login throttling, HTTPS/host restrictions, native authorization, bounded framing with receipt acknowledgement, and verification of the pipe server against the Windows mail-service PID. The Bootstrap preview exposes status, domain inspection, spam settings, DNSBL CRUD, saved SpamAssassin connection testing and SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS advice, including shared-provider SPF.

This is the first Phase 1b slice, not the completed replacement. The installer still selects the existing panel, and the native pipe is disabled unless a client SID is configured. Complete administration parity, final hosting/installer provisioning, SpamAssassin engine packaging and remaining DNS workflows follow after maintainer review.

Validation:
- Native service, API, tests and current Administrator compile successfully. Native/API builds have zero warnings.
- VM-only verification passed 26 deterministic DNS assertions, 54 HTTP/session assertions, 2 production HTTPS checks, 2 anti-squatting assertions and 18 live native/parser/permission assertions.
- VM browser checks passed navigation, DNSBL changes, SpamAssassin feedback, DNS guidance, logout and mobile layout.
- The existing 1,313-test VM run recorded 1,200 passes and three failures attributable to its old Administrator DLL and stale mail-data folder. All three targeted cases passed after aligning the tool and isolating mail data. The original VM database, executable, INI, environment and checkpoint were restored.
- CI now runs management security, DNS, browser and native integration tests in all three installed-database jobs. Fresh CI full-suite results are pending.
- Staged diff checks passed. Development-host execution is restricted to editing, static inspection and compilation; further runtime testing is VM/CI only.

Requirements, architecture, roadmap and agent instructions reflect the revised design. After this PR, wait for maintainer confirmation before the next task/phase/PR; continue monitoring and fixing this PR's CI. Do not merge without explicit approval.

+# Phase 1b management architecture
+
+## Decision (2026-10-26)
+
+The maintainer requested that the new administration panel avoid a COM backend. Build the new
+HTTP application on **ASP.NET Core / .NET 10**, alongside the existing .NET 10 tools. The new
+panel and REST API have **no COM dependency** and do not access the mail database directly.
+This supersedes the earlier PHP-hosted REST proposal and the PHP runtime requirement for the
+replacement panel. PHP remains relevant only to the existing legacy WebAdmin during migration.
+
+COM is not inherently insecure, and replacing it alone does not establish security. The goal
+is an explicit, testable management boundary with limited operations and least privilege.
+Retain the existing COM API separately for the Administrator, DBSetup, scripts and upgrade
+compatibility. Removing those consumers and COM registration is a separate migration; this
+change must not break them or silently expose them to the web application.
+
+Keeping COM for compatibility retains that existing attack surface. Do not grant the API
+identity DCOM access; audit legacy activation permissions independently. Migrating desktop tools,
+DB setup and scripts to the new API must precede any eventual removal of COM registration.
+
+## Boundaries
+
+```text
+Browser -> HTTPS REST /api/v1 -> ASP.NET Core administration process
+                                     |
+                          local Windows named pipe
+                                     |
+                          native management dispatcher
+                                     |
+                         C++ business / persistence layer
+
+Existing desktop tools / scripts -> existing COM API -> same business layer
+```
+
+- Host the API with its own restricted Windows identity. It must not run as LocalSystem or
+  an administrator, and needs no direct database credentials, mail-store access or DCOM grant.
+- The native management pipe is opt-in through `[Management] ApiClientSID` in `hMailServer.ini`
+  (or the mail service process environment setting `ARZOIEMAIL_MANAGEMENT_CLIENT_SID`, which
+  takes precedence). Use the dedicated API service identity's SID in production.
+  No network listener is added to the C++ mail service.
+- The pipe permits only the configured API identity, the mail service identity and SYSTEM.
+  Reject remote clients, reserve the first pipe instance, bound message size and depth, apply
+  I/O deadlines and stop the worker before closing the database. The client verifies that
+  the pipe server process is the running `hMailServer` service to resist name squatting.
+- Use a versioned, length-prefixed JSON command protocol, a client receipt acknowledgement before
+  pipe disconnect, and an explicit allowlist of operations.
+  Never expose arbitrary object traversal, reflection, SQL, shell commands or filesystem reads.
+- Authenticate credentials and authorize each operation in the native dispatcher. Share
+  credential validation with the compatibility interface, not its COM wrappers. Domain and
+  account boundaries must be enforced even if an HTTP handler is implemented incorrectly.
+
+## HTTP security
+
+- Use framework cookie protection and antiforgery, secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies, HTTPS,
+  login rate limits, request limits, strict CSP, generic errors and no permissive CORS policy.
+- Require explicit production `AllowedHosts` and HTTPS. Unencrypted HTTP is allowed only for
+  loopback connections in the Development environment, inside the test VM.
+- Cookies contain only opaque session IDs. Keep credentials encrypted in bounded, ephemeral
+  server-side memory, reauthenticate native commands and expire sessions on restart, logout,
+  inactivity or credential revocation. Never persist passwords in browser storage or cookies.
+- Do not trust forwarded headers without an explicitly configured trusted proxy. Production
+  deployments terminate HTTPS in the application or a configured trusted hosting layer.
+- Publish versioned REST documentation and test unauthenticated access, CSRF, role changes,
+  domain isolation, malformed IPC, pipe ACLs, unavailable services and credential revocation.
+
+## Delivery status
+
+The maintainer requires **all runtime testing inside the disposable Hyper-V VM or CI**, including
+unit/security test executables, browser previews and integration tests. The development host is
+for source editing, static inspection and compilation only. Do not start a local API preview or
+run test executables there. This supersedes earlier local-testing notes and assumptions.
+
+Implementation is in progress on `feature/webadmin-rest-foundation`. The uncommitted PHP/COM
+prototype was withdrawn; reusable Bootstrap assets are retained under
+`hmailserver/source/Management/Api/wwwroot`. New backend code is under `Management/Api` and
+native management code belongs under `Server/Common/Management`.
+
+Deliver and validate the native transport/authentication and HTTP foundation first, then migrate
+administration capabilities and DNS guidance with regression coverage. Do not switch the installer
+to the replacement panel or claim complete parity until endpoint, browser and upgrade tests pass.
+SpamAssassin integration, DNSBL control and complex SPF/DKIM/DMARC guidance remain required.
+Engine bundling and final service/installer provisioning remain explicit delivery work.
+
+## Implementation sequence
+
+1. Establish the opt-in native management boundary, shared business authentication, ASP.NET Core
+   session/security foundation, initial spam/DNSBL/DNS workflows and repeatable tests. This is
+   the current foundation change; it does not switch existing installations to the new panel.
+2. Migrate the remaining domain/account, alias, distribution-list, delivery, rules, TLS and
+   advanced administration capabilities to explicit native commands and REST endpoints, with
+   server/domain/account permission tests for every operation.
+3. Complete DNS setup workflows and protocol-conformance coverage, including DKIM key lifecycle
+   and provider coexistence. Retain the distinction between DNS inspection and message-level
+   authentication; do not replace the server's existing authentication evaluators with the wizard.
+4. Finalize SpamAssassin engine packaging/lifecycle, API hosting under a restricted identity,
+   HTTPS/certificate provisioning and offline installer/runtime delivery.
+5. Switch the installer and end-user documentation only after parity, upgrade, security and
+   supported-database acceptance tests pass. Retire the legacy PHP panel through that migration;
+   keep COM compatibility independent until its consumers have a supported replacement.

+# ArzoieMail management API and panel (Phase 1b, in progress)
+
+The replacement panel is an ASP.NET Core / .NET 10 application. It communicates with the native
+server over a restricted local Windows named pipe, never through COM or direct SQL. The old
+PHP application and COM API remain available as compatibility surfaces during migration.
+
+Read [the requirements](../../../docs/webadmin-requirements.md) and
+[architecture/security boundaries](../../../docs/management-api-architecture.md).
+
+## Build on the development host
+
+```
+dotnet build hmailserver/source/Management/Api/ArzoieMail.Api.csproj -c Release
+dotnet build hmailserver/source/Management/Tests/ArzoieMail.Management.Tests.csproj -c Release
+```
+
+Build the C++ server using `build/build.ps1`. A full server build is required for changes to
+the native management channel. Do not register it or install it on the development host.
+
+**Run all test executables, application previews and browser tests only in the disposable VM
+or CI.** `build/test-management.ps1` checks for a VM before executing tests. Test sources live
+in `hmailserver/test/RegressionTests/Management`; they compile into a separate test executable.
+
+## Deployment design
+
+- Publish `Api/ArzoieMail.Api.csproj` for Windows x64. The ASP.NET Core runtime is required,
+  or publish a self-contained bundle. The Desktop Runtime alone does not provide ASP.NET Core.
+- Use a separate restricted service or IIS application-pool identity. Do not grant DCOM,
+  administrator, database or mail-store access to this identity.
+- Set `[Management] ApiClientSID` in the mail server's protected `hMailServer.ini` to that
+  identity's SID, then restart the mail service. Leave the value absent to disable the pipe.
+- Configure an explicit administration hostname with `AllowedHosts` and a valid HTTPS binding.
+  No wildcard hosts, permissive CORS policy or automatic trust of forwarded headers is enabled.
+- The API checks the named-pipe server PID against the running mail service before sending
+  credentials. Both native and HTTP layers enforce the management boundary.
+- The API identity needs permission to query the mail service's status for that verification;
+  it does not need service start/stop or administrator permission.
+- Web credentials are kept encrypted in bounded ephemeral memory; cookies hold only opaque
+  session IDs. Logout, process restart, inactivity and credential revocation invalidate sessions.
+- Installer/service provisioning and complete legacy-page parity are still being implemented.
+  This preview is not yet selected by the installer as the replacement for existing WebAdmin.
+
+## REST v1 contract
+
+Responses use `{ "data": ... }`, or `{ "error": { "message": "..." } }` for errors.
+POST/PATCH/DELETE requests require JSON, a same-origin request and an `X-CSRF-Token` header.
+GET `/api/v1/session` supplies the initial antiforgery token. Obtain the new token after login
+or logout. Cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure in production. Sessions expire after
+30 minutes of inactivity, with an eight-hour absolute limit and no persistence across restart.
+
+| Method | Endpoint | Native operation / permissions |
+|---|---|---|
+| GET | `/api/v1/session` | Anonymous bootstrap or current authenticated identity |
+| POST | `/api/v1/session` | Sign in with username/password; rate limited |
+| DELETE | `/api/v1/session` | Sign out |
+| GET | `/api/v1/status` | Server administrator |
+| GET | `/api/v1/domains` | Server scope or the caller's own domain |
+| POST | `/api/v1/domains/{id}/dns` | Native domain authorization, then DNS advice; domain/server administrator |
+| GET / PATCH | `/api/v1/antispam` | Server administrator; explicit allowlisted fields |
+| GET / POST | `/api/v1/dnsbl` | List/create providers; server administrator |
+| PATCH / DELETE | `/api/v1/dnsbl/{id}` | Update/delete provider; server administrator |
+| POST | `/api/v1/spamassassin/test` | Test saved host/port; server administrator |
+| GET | `/api/v1/diagnostics` | Server administrator |
+
+DNSBL creation accepts `Active` (boolean), `DNSHost`, `ExpectedResult`, `RejectMessage`
+(strings), and `Score` (integer 0..10000). All five fields are required. PATCH accepts a subset.
+Unknown properties and incorrect types are refused before writes. DNSBLs created through the
+panel start disabled. Spam settings persist individually in the existing server; validation
+finishes before writes, but multi-setting updates are not a database transaction.
+
+DNS inspection accepts `addresses` and `includes` arrays (up to ten each), `selector`, and an
+optional base64 RSA `publicKey` (at least 2048 bits). It preserves existing SPF policies when
+proposing a merge, detects include/redirect cycles and lookup-budget overflow, and labels
+sender-dependent/macros or DNS failures inconclusive. It does not claim full message-context
+SPF evaluation, organizational-domain DMARC inheritance, or proof of outgoing DKIM signing.
+DNS is read through the Windows resolver, not a third-party public service. Review proposals
+and test messages from all providers before strengthening DMARC.

+"""Browser interaction tests with explicit network fixtures; native/API tests run separately."""
+import json
+import pathlib
+import sys
+from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
+
+base = sys.argv[1].rstrip('/')
+output = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
+output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+providers = [{"id": 1, "Active": True, "DNSHost": "dnsbl.example.net", "ExpectedResult": "127.0.0.*", "RejectMessage": "Blocked", "Score": 3}]
+user = {"address": "Administrator", "level": 2, "domainId": 0, "accountId": 0}
+settings = {"SpamAssassinEnabled": True, "SpamAssassinHost": "127.0.0.1", "SpamAssassinPort": 783, "SpamAssassinMergeScore": True, "SpamAssassinScore": 5, "UseSPF": True, "UseSPFScore": 3, "DMARCEnabled": True, "SpamMarkThreshold": 5, "SpamDeleteThreshold": 20}
+requests = []
+
+
+def api(route):
+    global user
+    request = route.request
+    path = request.url.split('/api/v1', 1)[1]
+    body = json.loads(request.post_data or '{}')
+    requests.append((request.method, path, body))
+    data = {}
+    if path == '/session':
+        if request.method == 'DELETE':
+            user = None
+        data = {"user": user, "csrf": "browser-fixture-token"}
+    elif path == '/status':
+        data = {"version": "5.7.2", "state": 3, "domains": 2}
+    elif path == '/dnsbl':
+        if request.method == 'POST':
+            providers.append({"id": len(providers) + 1, **body})
+            data = providers[-1]
+        else:
+            data = {"items": providers}
+    elif path.startswith('/dnsbl/'):
+        item = next(v for v in providers if v['id'] == int(path.rsplit('/', 1)[1]))
+        if request.method == 'DELETE':
+            providers.remove(item)
+            data = {"deleted": True}
+        else:
+            item.update(body)
+            data = item
+    elif path == '/antispam':
+        settings.update(body)
+        data = settings
+    elif path == '/domains':
+        data = {"items": [{"id": 5, "name": "example.com", "active": True, "dkimEnabled": True, "selector": "arzoie"}]}
+    elif path.endswith('/dns'):
+        record = {"name": "example.com", "type": "TXT", "published": "v=spf1 include:provider.example -all", "proposed": "v=spf1 include:provider.example ip4:203.0.113.10 -all", "status": "valid", "errors": [], "warnings": []}
+        data = {"domain": "example.com", "spf": record,
+                "dkim": {**record, "name": "arzoie._domainkey.example.com", "published": ["v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=[public key]"], "proposed": None},
+                "dmarc": {**record, "name": "_dmarc.example.com", "published": ["v=DMARC1; p=none; adkim=r; aspf=r"], "proposed": None},
+                "notice": "DNS inspection only; message alignment needs testing."}
+    elif path == '/diagnostics':
+        data = {"checks": [{"safe": True, "message": "Native management channel connected; no COM dependency."}]}
+    elif path == '/spamassassin/test':
+        data = {"connected": True}
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected browser API call: {request.method} {path}")
+    route.fulfill(status=200, content_type='application/json', body=json.dumps({"data": data}))
+
+
+with sync_playwright() as p:
+    browser = p.chromium.launch(channel='msedge', headless=True)
+    page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 1000})
+    errors = []
+    page.on('pageerror', lambda error: errors.append(str(error)))
+    page.route('**/api/v1/**', api)
+    page.goto(base)
+    page.get_by_text('Running', exact=True).wait_for()
+    page.screenshot(path=str(output / 'overview-desktop.png'), full_page=True)
+    page.get_by_role('link', name='DNS blocklists').click()
+    page.get_by_text('dnsbl.example.net', exact=True).wait_for()
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Disable', exact=True).click()
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Enable', exact=True).wait_for()
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Add provider').click()
+    page.get_by_label('DNSHost').fill('second.example.net')
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Save changes').click()
+    page.get_by_text('second.example.net', exact=True).wait_for()
+    assert providers[-1]['Active'] is False, 'New providers must start disabled.'
+    page.screenshot(path=str(output / 'dnsbl-desktop.png'), full_page=True)
+    page.get_by_role('link', name='Spam protection').click()
+    page.get_by_label('Spam Assassin Host', exact=True).wait_for()
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Test saved connection').click()
+    page.get_by_text('SpamAssassin connection succeeded.', exact=True).wait_for()
+    page.get_by_role('link', name='Domains & DNS').click()
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Inspect DNS').click()
+    page.get_by_label('Sending IP addresses (comma separated)').fill('203.0.113.10')
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Validate published DNS & build recommendations').click()
+    page.get_by_text('DNS inspection only; message alignment needs testing.', exact=True).wait_for()
+    assert requests[-1][2]['addresses'] == ['203.0.113.10']
+    page.screenshot(path=str(output / 'dns-desktop.png'), full_page=True)
+    page.set_viewport_size({"width": 390, "height": 844})
+    page.screenshot(path=str(output / 'dns-mobile.png'), full_page=True)
+    assert page.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth'), 'Mobile page overflows horizontally.'
+    page.get_by_role('button', name='Sign out').click()
+    page.get_by_role('heading', name='Sign in to your server').wait_for()
+    page.screenshot(path=str(output / 'login-mobile.png'), full_page=True)
+    assert not errors, errors
+    browser.close()
+print('Passed browser navigation, DNSBL mutation, SpamAssassin test, DNS guidance, logout and mobile layout checks.')

commit.message:
Introduce a native management API and modern panel foundation

Build the replacement panel on ASP.NET Core/.NET 10 with a versioned REST
API and a restricted local named-pipe boundary into the C++ business layer.
Keep COM as an independent compatibility adapter, sharing authentication
without using COM from the new API.

Add protected sessions, CSRF and origin checks, login throttling, explicit
native authorization, initial spam/DNSBL controls and DNS setup guidance.
Cover the boundary with VM-only HTTP, DNS, browser, anti-squatting and live
native tests, and run the new suites in the database CI jobs. Record the
architecture, staged delivery and the maintainer's per-PR review gate.

Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>

Handle empty installer credentials in management CI setup

A fresh silent install keeps the administrator password empty. Preserve
that existing setup credential with an empty SecureString instead of
passing an empty string to ConvertTo-SecureString, which rejects it.
Reproduced the failure and verified the corrected path inside the VM.

Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>

Wait for restore completion without comparing second-resolution timestamps

The internal-database CI restore completed and restarted the server in the
same second as its previous start. Wait for fresh restore-completion and
server-started log messages instead of a changed Status.StartTime string.
Keep the existing timeout and fail immediately on a reported restore error.

Verified all five backup-passphrase tests and the management security/native
suites inside the disposable VM; restored the VM checkpoint afterward.

Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>

issue.title: Document TLS, high-pressure Defender scanning and PHP retirement

repository.name: ArzoieMail
repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
Define the remaining Phase 1b certificate experience: guided import or automatic issuance, SMTP/IMAP/POP3 listener assignment, validation, expiry and renewal status, safe activation and rollback. Keep IIS HTTPS bindings separate from mail TLS and require restricted native operations for private-key handling.

Add optional Microsoft Defender Antivirus scanning with a feasibility assessment grounded in existing message/decoded-attachment scan hooks and Microsoft documentation. Cover high-pressure receiving, submission, queued sending, server-saved IMAP drafts, imports and intermediate content versions. Require durable scan scheduling, bounded workers, verdict gates, backpressure, fair scheduling, idempotent mitigation and crash recovery. Explicitly distinguish client-local drafts from uploaded content and scheduler recovery guarantees from ambiguous remote SMTP acceptance.

Require at least 10,000 queued/in-flight messages in VM acceptance, mixed lifecycle traffic, burst/outage/restart/soak scenarios and published throughput, latency and resource measurements. Local Defender capacity is conditional on those results; these documents do not claim an implemented or benchmarked scanner.

Make full PHP retirement the agreed end state after feature parity and migration acceptance, including legacy source, packaging, runtime requirements and the old administration endpoint. Keep README, roadmap, requirements and architecture aligned with the merged PR #31 foundation and remaining delivery work.

Refresh shared project memory in AGENTS.md and docs/agents: replace stale handoff status, link the current plan/tracker, preserve the maintainer’s review gate and VM/CI-only runtime rule, and clearly separate merged work from planned or unverified functionality.

Validation: reviewed documentation, repository integration points, Microsoft primary sources and internal references; git diff --check passed. Documentation only; no application code changed and no runtime tests executed on the development host. CI pending for the latest head. Implementation and VM validation remain future work.
